title: The changes from #11292 seem to break opening links in descendant `<iframe>`
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I'm implementing the changes from #11292 in Servo. These changes cause the following tests to fail:

```
  ▶ OK /html/browsers/the-window-object/window-open-noopener.html?indexed
  │   ▶ FAIL [expected PASS] window.open() with 'noopener' should reuse existing target
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] noopener=1 means the same as noopener
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] noopener separated only by spaces should work
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] Trailing noopener should work
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] Leading noopener should work
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] Interior noopener should work
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ FAIL [expected PASS] noreferrer should also suppress opener when reusing existing target
  │   │   → assert_equals: Should still have opener expected true but got false
  │   │ 
  │   │ indexedTests/</channel.onmessage<@http://web-platform.test:8000/html/browsers/the-window-object/window-open-noopener.html?indexed:92:24
  │   │ Test.prototype.step@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2869:25
  └   └ Test.prototype.step_func_done/<@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2944:32

  ▶ OK /html/semantics/links/links-created-by-a-and-area-elements/htmlanchorelement_noopener.html
  │   ▶ FAIL [expected PASS] Check that targeting of rel=noopener with a given name reuses an existing subframe with that name
  │   │   → assert_true: expected true got false
  │   │ 
  │   │ channel.onmessage<@http://web-platform.test:8000/html/semantics/links/links-created-by-a-and-area-elements/htmlanchorelement_noopener.html:70:14
  │   │ Test.prototype.step@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2869:25
  └   └ Test.prototype.step_func_done/<@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2944:32

  ▶ TIMEOUT /html/browsers/windows/noreferrer-window-name.html
  │   ▶ PASS [expected TIMEOUT] Following a noreferrer link with a named target should not cause creation of a window that can be targeted by another noreferrer link with the same named target
  │   │ TIMEOUT [expected PASS] Targeting a rel=noreferrer link at an existing named subframe should work
  │   └   → Test timed out
  │   ▶ FAIL [expected PASS] Targeting a rel=noreferrer link at an existing named window should work
  │   │   → assert_equals: expected false but got true
  │   │ 
  │   │ channel.onmessage<@http://web-platform.test:8000/html/browsers/windows/noreferrer-window-name.html:91:20
  │   │ Test.prototype.step@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2869:25
  └   └ Test.prototype.step_func_done/<@http://web-platform.test:8000/resources/testharness.js:2944:32
```

The presumptive reason:  `<a target="myframe" rel="noopener">` in a page containing `<iframe name="myframe">` opens a new top-level window instead of navigating the `<iframe>`.

Perhaps the case this change was already covered by step 8.7 of "find a navigable with name" which covers browsing context groups. I'm not sure as we haven't gotten this far with the implementation in Servo.
